identity.name: KPEL
identity.industry: Wind-power EPC & Balance-of-Plant / grid-evacuation infrastructure (renewable energy transition)

summary.oneLiner: India's only end-to-end integrated wind/hybrid EPC + BOP + transmission + O&M player, riding a record order book (2.18 GW / ~INR 2,600 cr) but heavily reliant on captive affiliate KPI Green (~70% of book) and still waiting on the long-promised external/Gujarat order breakthrough.

one-line thesis: India's only end-to-end integrated wind/hybrid EPC + BOP + transmission + O&M player, riding a record order book (2.18 GW / ~INR 2,600 cr) but heavily reliant on captive affiliate KPI Green (~70% of book) and still waiting on the long-promised external/Gujarat order breakthrough.
financial scorecard (consolidated): Highest-ever Q3 revenue. Margins expanding modestly; PAT growth (+57%) trails EBITDA (+75%) — implied higher interest/depreciation/tax (IPP ramp). No one-offs flagged. CFO confirmed 9M operating cash flow positive. Note: EPC revenue this quarter ~INR 328 cr, of which ~INR 250+ cr (≈76%) from KPI Green.
guidance (verify next quarter): Q4 FY26: guided to be the "highest Q4 ever"; analyst math implied ~INR 550–600 cr top line (mgmt did not deny, said "we will definitely achieve a larger number" — soft confirmation, not committed).
Growth: reiterated 50–60% (analyst said up to 60–70%) YoY revenue growth for FY26 and the following year, backed by 2.18 GW book and 12–18 month execution runway.
New orders: CEO stated explicitly new hybrid/BOS orders to be booked "this quarter" (Q4 FY26) — KEY ITEM TO VERIFY next call (this has slipped 2–3 quarters already).
IPP: target 100 MW IPP by FY27-28; 48.5 MW done, balance 51.5 MW; "near future" news promised.
order book & pipeline: Current order book ~2.18 GW, all CPP (captive power plant) projects, ~INR 2,600+ cr value; execution over 12–18 (some up to 24) months.
Mix: ~70% (~INR 1,800–1,850 cr) from KPI Green; ~30% non-KPI.
Fresh bid pipeline ~100 MW direct competitive bidding + ~700–800 MW non-bid (EPC + BOS supply contracts); CEO summarised "near about 500 MW" KPE-concentrated pipeline. New bids are non-KPI.
Caution: per-MW realization NOT a clean divide vs order book — revenue is percentage-of-completion; rough WTG+small-EHV scope ~INR 7.5–8 cr/MW including turbine.
segment / subsidiary: Group has three listed entities: engineering/manufacturing arm; KPI Green Energy (solar-led, IPP-heavy, strong market cap, holds BESS); KP Energy (this co., wind EPC/BOP).
Hybrid logic: wind portion of group hybrid projects routed to KP Energy; solar/IPP & BESS sit in KPI Green.
Mgmt firmly rejected an analyst's KPI+KPE merger suggestion — argues distinct verticals need separate teams (SBI analogy). Related-party intensity acknowledged but defended.
growth verticals / optionality: Offshore/near-shore wind: GoI 1 GW offshore-by-2030 directive; Gujarat & Tamil Nadu RFQs under prep with MNRE; projects take 3–5 yrs, movement "next year onwards." Optionality, not near-term.
Botswana: MOU to build 500 MW first, then scale to 5 GW by 2030 (group/KPI-level framing).
IPP build-out at KPEL to 100 MW (FY27-28) — adds annuity/terminal value.
Repowering: 25–30 GW ageing-wind repowering TAM cited.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin ~22%, up ~150 bps YoY. Key raw material = turbines (price hedged/locked at order booking) + structures/evacuation lines (inventory pre-stocked; price-escalation clauses pass-through beyond threshold). Mgmt downplayed tariff/commodity risk to margins.
capex / expansion: IPP capex self-funding from internal accruals + recently raised warrants (equity already partly infused). No turbine-manufacturing capex (asset-light EPC + selective IPP).
capital allocation: "No dilution needed at present"; cash flows "very good," internal accruals sufficient. Warrant proceeds earmarked partly for IPP. Contrasted with KPI's INR 1,000 cr QIP that drew FIIs.
risks & watch-items: Affiliate concentration: ~70% of book and ~76% of Q3 EPC revenue from KPI Green — captive/related-party dependence is the central risk.
Repeatedly slipping external orders: street has awaited a fresh order for 2–3 quarters; deferred on Gujarat policy/connectivity procedures. Now promised "this quarter."
Lumpy POC revenue makes per-MW economics opaque.
Q4 guidance soft — implied INR 550–600 cr not firmly committed.
Offshore wind is multi-year, low near-term contribution.
Low institutional (FII/DII) ownership vs KPI; mgmt sees it as market-cap-gated.
management quality / tone: Confident, execution-focused, slightly promotional ("hard to replicate platform," "28 IIM-A alumni"). CFO articulate and consistent; CEO direct on order timing. Open about KPI dependence and answered tough merger/RPT and per-MW questions without evasion. Repeated reassurance pattern on guidance suggests street skepticism on order delivery.
non-obvious takeaways: KPEL is effectively the captive wind-EPC arm of the KP Group's IPP ambitions — its growth is mechanically tied to KPI Green's solar/hybrid IPP capex cycle, so KPEL's order book is partly an internal transfer, not pure external market share.
Fast execution is doubly incentivized: it books KPEL EPC revenue AND accelerates KPI's IPP revenue — alignment, but also circularity.
Repowering (25–30 GW) and offshore are real multi-year optionality the market may underprice, but neither is in numbers yet.
BESS terminal-value upside sits in KPI, NOT KPEL — investors conflating the two would mis-value KPEL.
qoq change log: First note in this tracking series for KPEL — no prior-quarter baseline. Establishes Q3 FY26 baseline: revenue INR 347.6 cr, EBITDA INR 77.2 cr (~22% margin), PAT INR 41.3 cr, order book 2.18 GW (~INR 2,600 cr, ~70% KPI), IPP 48.5 MW, O&M 644+ MW.

Open items to track next quarter: (a) did the promised "this-quarter" external/hybrid/BOS order materialize; (b) Q4 revenue vs implied INR 550–600 cr; (c) IPP progress toward 100 MW; (d) non-KPI order-book share trend; (e) Botswana 500 MW progress.

themes.title: Power transmission & renewable-evacuation capex
themes.need: Grid build-out to evacuate ~90 GW of new renewables is the broadest theme in the universe - pulling EHV/765kV transmission EPC, towers, conductors, OPGW, cables and HVDC. POWERGRID/ADANIENSOL TBCB pipeline plus state RDSS/underground-cabling capex (Rajesh Power 544291, OMPOWER) underpins multi-year visibility for EPC, tower (KP Green 544150, SKIPPER) and conductor/cable makers (KEI, RRKABEL, DYCL).
themes.driver: Fresh TBCB awards + execution ramp; EPC order inflows over next 1-2 quarters.

themes.title: Renewable IPP / FDRE firm-power & storage
themes.need: DISCOMs mandating firm/round-the-clock RE make BESS + pumped-hydro the bid differentiator, and in Q1FY27 storage demand ran ahead of supply. ADANIGREEN has 3.5 GWh of BESS installed (+1.9 GWh at Khavda this quarter), targets 10+ GWh this fiscal and 50 GWh by FY30 on a thumb-rule INR 25-30 lakh of EBITDA per MWh against ~INR 1.5cr/MWh of capex, and has contracted essentially all merchant/C&I capacity to sibling AESL on 25-year (solar/wind) and 15-year (battery) fixed-price PPAs targeting ~15-16% IRR - a pivot from merchant builder to fixed-return contracted IPP, with evacuation (not panels) named as the binding constraint. JSWENERGY added 873 MW in Q1 and ~1.1 GW since April - 36% of its 3 GW FY27 target already banked, Tidong Hydro commissioned four months early - and raised INR 10,150cr, taking net leverage 5.2x to 4.95x. On the equipment side SERVOTECH said its BESS pack capacity is fully booked ('we are not able to meet the demand') and committed to 2x capacity in 6 months, 3x by 21-Mar-2027 and 10x within 2 years. ACMESOLAR/KPIGREEN/SUZLON/INOXWIND attach storage to solar/wind; NTPC/NHPC/SJVN/TATAPOWER drive pumped-hydro and utility-scale storage.
themes.driver: BESS capacity commissioning against demand two independent managements (ADANIGREEN, SERVOTECH) say already exceeds supply; FDRE/peak-power tender awards; merchant DAM prices (JSWENERGY: INR 4.40 -> INR 5.10/unit, +16%) on +8.5% Q1 power demand.
